generation: Speed Concept 2nd generation (rim brake, mono riser cockpit, MY2014 to about 2021)
identify: Rim brakes and quick-release wheels, no IsoSpeed; a proprietary direct-mount stem with the basebar bolted on from below and a single mono riser ('pedestal') carrying the arm-pad wing and mono extension. Announced Sept 2013 for MY2014; Trek says parts interchange across 2014–2020. The 2022+ SLR has disc brakes and two towers; the 2010–2013 bike is a different first generation.

cockpit.steerer: Not verified (proprietary front end; no Trek spec sheet found).
cockpit.stem: Proprietary direct-mount stem in six versions: Low/Medium/High height, each Near or Far. The basebar ('pursuit bar') bolts up through the stem from underneath, with 10 mm of fore-aft adjustment.
cockpit.stack_system: Stem height (Low/Medium/High; Trek: over 14 cm of height adjustment per size across the stems) plus a mono riser/pedestal in four heights 10 mm apart and a 5 mm spacer under the pad wing. Owners and Trek cite riser stacks such as 15 mm (smallest), 35+5 and 45+5 mm.
cockpit.reach_system: Near/Far stem choice; mono extension and pad wing sit in different hole sets; the pad wing can be flipped 180° for more or less reach; pads also slide on the wing.
cockpit.angle_system: Tilt cradle angles pads and extensions upward (range not published). Aftermarket adapters add fixed or adjustable tilt (AeroCoach 15–27°, Wattshop 5–25°).
cockpit.notes: Extensions come in four Trek styles (S-bend, straight, ergo, short ergo), cut to length, about 40 mm of fore-aft adjustment once fitted. The Mono Plug-In accepts extensions of the rider's choice (22.2 mm). Owners call the front end a lot of work to fit (many proprietary stems/risers), swapping risers awkward with mechanical shifting, and proprietary stems for extreme fits now hard to find. A newer plug-in/slider moved from 5 mm to 6 mm hardware.

parts.model: Speed Concept direct-mount stem (Low / Medium / High × Near / Far)

effect.text: The main stack/reach lever on this generation: six stems give over 14 cm of height adjustment per frame size (Trek), with Near/Far versions for reach. Exact per-stem offsets were not found.

evidence.says: 2013 launch coverage: six stem options (low/medium/high, each near/far) give over 14 cm height adjustment per size; base bar 10 mm fore-aft adjustment.
Trek's community manager suggests a High-Far stem plus 45 mm of spacers to raise pads on a size M, and says 2014–2020 Speed Concept parts are interchangeable.
2024 owners trade Gen 2 stems and monorisers second-hand (Low/Near stem part #436145); a Low/Far stem was sought.

parts.needs: Brake/shift cables re-routed; parts now mostly second-hand.

parts.model: Speed Concept mono riser / pedestals and 5 mm spacer

effect.text: Four pedestal heights 10 mm apart plus a 5 mm spacer under the pad wing: about 35 mm of pad stack on a given stem. Owners report 15 mm as the smallest riser and Trek cites a 45+5 mm combination.

evidence.says: 2015 article on the Speed Concept fit chart (adapted from Trek's engineer): one pedestal on the pursuit bar, four options each 10 mm taller, plus a 5 mm spacer under the pad wing.
Trek's community manager: an XL with a 45+5 mm mono and a Far-Near stem hits a 740 mm pad stack / 555 mm reach.
Owner on a size L runs the smallest 15 mm riser and says swapping risers is awkward with mechanical shifting.

parts.needs: Longer bolts for taller risers; cable re-routing with mechanical shifting.

effect.text: Replaces the one-piece mono extension so standard 22.2 mm extensions of the rider's choice plug into its ends; this is how Gen 2 owners fit longer or different-shape bars. An owner says pad stack does not change versus stock even with longer poles. It has three pad-mounting holes per side, versus four on the S-bend mono.

evidence.says: Trek's community manager: the Mono Plug-In lets a bar of your choice be installed into the ends; new version uses Mono Plugin W582446, 6 mm bolt/T-nut 596164 and Mono Slider W582447.
Bontrager Speed Concept mono extension family for the 2014 (Gen 2) bike, accepts standard 22.2 mm extensions, internally routed for Di2 or cable.
Owner: with the plug-in, elbow-pad stack stays the same as standard even with longer poles.

parts.needs: Your own 22.2 mm extensions; check old (5 mm) versus new (6 mm) hardware before mixing parts. Owners noted EU supply delays.

parts.model: Speed Concept mono extensions (S-bend, straight, Ergo, Ergo Long – W582443)

effect.text: Trek's own one-piece mono extensions in four shapes; cut to length and about 40 mm of fore-aft adjustment once fitted. Changes hand position, not pad position.

evidence.says: Launch coverage: four extension styles (s-bend, straight, ergo, short ergo), can be cut, up to 40 mm adjustment once fixed.
Mono Ergo Long described as designed for second-generation Speed Concept (2014 onwards) (search result; page refused connection).
Trek's community manager: owners can swap the mono extension for a long-reach or plug-in version for more length; keep the set screw in place.

parts.model: Ascalon adapter – Trek Speed Concept (rim brake, monopost), tilt adjustable / low stack

effect.text: Mounts AeroCoach Ascalon extensions on the Gen 2 mono riser at a 15° base angle, tiltable up to 27°; a separate low-stack version is listed. No Trek-specific pad numbers published.

evidence.says: Lists Trek Speed Concept (rim brake) monopost adapter, 15° base tiltable to 27°, plus a rim-brake low-stack tilt-adjustable option; works only with Ascalon extensions.
Gen 2 owner notes the Ascalon has an adapter but a BTA bottle would need extra hardware.

parts.needs: AeroCoach Ascalon extensions (sold separately). Price = £115 base + £252.50 rim-brake option, incl. UK VAT.

parts.model: Adapter plate for Trek Speed Concept mono riser (with FastTT aero bars)

effect.text: Mounts FastTT full-arm bars on the Gen 2 mono riser; reversible with integrated BTA mount. One owner found the pads sit lower than stock (went up one riser) and the overall position longer.

evidence.says: FastTT plate for the Trek Speed Concept mono riser, used with FastTT aero bars, reversible, integrated BTA mount, CAD 182 (search result; page rate-limited when opened).
Gen 2 owner fitted the FastTT plate and extensions, very pleased; pads sit lower so he added one riser; fit came out longer.
2018 Gen 2 owner lists the FastTT mono-riser adapter among options.

parts.needs: FastTT aero bars (sold separately); BTA needs extra hardware per one owner.

effect.text: Full extension system offered for mono-riser basebars 'like that on the Trek Speed Concept'; angled risers 5–25° in 5° steps, adjustable reach and width via mounting plates; replaces the mono riser plus pad plate per a Gen 2 owner.

evidence.says: 2020 launch report: Anemoi available for standard dual-mount or mono-riser base bars like the Trek Speed Concept; 5–25° risers; from £1,495 at launch.
2018 Gen 2 owner leans towards the Anemoi mono-bracket adapter because it replaces the mono riser and horizontal plate.

parts.needs: Confirm the Speed Concept mono-riser bracket with Wattshop before ordering.

effect.text: Made for the 2022+ disc bike's arm-pad bracket only.

parts.reason_incompatible: Designed for the Gen 3 (disc, twin-post) Speed Concept arm-pad bracket; not for the Gen 1/2 rim-brake mono-riser cockpit.

evidence.says: Install guide applies only to the Trek Speed Concept disc brake, twin post, 2022+.
Speed Concept version compatible only with Gen 3 disc-brake bikes, not Gen 1 or 2 rim-brake ones (search result).

effect.text: Trek version mounts on the twin risers of the disc bike only.

parts.reason_incompatible: TriRig's Trek plate works only with Speed Concept disc (twin-post) frames; the rim-brake bike has a single mono riser.

evidence.says: Plate designed specifically for the Trek Speed Concept Twin Post (disc brake); sits on the two risers.
Listing says the Trek plate only works with Speed Concept disc frames (search result; page rate-limited when opened).
